verses.text: How terrible it will be for you who are comfortable in Zion and for you who feel safe on the hill of Samaria! You are the famous leaders of the greatest nation, the ones the people of Israel come to for help.
Go to Calneh and look. From there go to the great city of Hamath, and then go down to Gath in Philistia. Are they better than your two kingdoms? Is their land larger than yours?
You try to push away the day of disaster, but you bring near a time when violence will rule.
You lie on beds decorated with ivory and stretch out on your couches. You eat the best lambs from the flock and the finest calves from the stall.
You make up songs on your harps, and like David you invent musical instruments for yourselves.
You drink wine by the bowlful and put on the finest lotions, but you are not upset about the ruin of Joseph.
So you will be among the first to go into exile. Your feasting and lounging will come to an end.
The Lord GOD has sworn by himself. The LORD God of Armies says: "I hate the pride of Jacob, and I despise his fortresses. I will hand over the city and everything in it to the enemy."
If ten people are left in one house, they will all die.

And if a relative who is to burn the bodies comes to carry them out of the house, he will call to anyone hiding inside, "Is anyone else with you?" When the answer comes, "No," he will say, "Hush! We must not even mention the name of the LORD."
For the LORD has given the command. The great houses will be smashed to pieces, and the small houses broken into bits.
Do horses run on rocky cliffs? Does anyone plow the sea with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of doing right into bitterness.
You celebrate the capture of Lo Debar, a thing of nothing, and you say, "Didn't we take Karnaim by our own strength?"
"But I will stir up a nation against you, people of Israel," says the LORD God of Armies. "They will oppress you all the way from Lebo Hamath to the Valley of the Arabah."
